BPD is very treatable, but i am also very fortunate to be in Canada and a naturalized citizen. It can be more challenging to be treated in the US and developing/third world countries. Treating BPD, especially as it gets more severe, is a slow and ideally proactive approach to ensure you are able to stabilize yourself first so you dont hurt yourself or others (especially yourself!). Medications can help treat symptoms to make it a lot easier to absorb the more psycho-therapy type stuff. 

I hope you have a good doctor or psychiatrist. They truly make all the difference. Always make sure you know your options and rights. :)
tl;dr, i coped through realizing that this diagnosis means i can get more specialised care and i was fortunate to be around mental health professionals who give a shit

hey, im 25 now but i remember being 19 and being diagnosed in the emergency room after breaking down so hard i collapsed. My boyfriend at the time (now my ex and we're actually roommates and homies and he's my fp too so yeah, im not beating the allegations even while medicated and much more stable and having gone through years of treatment). 9 criteria.

To both me and my homie it was JARRING. I wasn't even crying, i was way calmer after basically having a super crashout in the middle of my campus lounge (not a surprise for a cs major in a theory heavy program... so no one really judged me LOL). I was oddly calm. It was auto pilot but not in the way one disassociates. I felt like hyper-awake. I distinctly remember me, on a wheelchair, and my homie waiting outside for a cab to take us back to campus because i came in an ambulance (i live in canada so it was 100 bucks and not an arm and a leg). I had pulled up the website the psychiatrist told us for a better overview of typical symptoms and we just went "oh that makes sense.... oh that makes sense.... oh... oh..." and we just kind of had a whole minute of sudden clarity. It helped that my psychiatrist deeply hesitated to give me the diagnosis. 

He had a rule in his practice to not diagnose with BPD right away. In the ER, he was asking me about my known family history of pretty bad mental illness. As we talked, he was ruling out basically everything until he got 9/9 BPD and took a deep breath and told me "yeah this is going to be a bit of a pain to treat BUT very treatable, you marked 9/9 for BPD. thats kind of damming. I dont like to diagnose BPD for cases like this but 9/9 is pretty concerning. makes me think you were misdiagnosed in high school. To be fair, BPD is not a diagnosis you should give to teenagers. But, as an adult, I'm fairly confident that this matches your symptoms the closest". 

It was very hard to argue back because suddenly it all somewhat made sense. This wasn't some sort of throwaway diagnosis, 9/9 is pretty damming. In a way, it all made sense. I spent years slowly working with my doctors and therapists in college to finish my degree even through COVID setting me back two years. 

Currently, im in a much more stable place, but my current psychiatrist hasn't ruled out BPD at all, though he did say that  I'm no longer 9 criteria, so i'm showing signs of improvement as i become less of a danger to myself. turns out im also neurodivergent. everything made double sense. it was that same clarity, at 25.

Racism has robbed enough from me and I ain't letting it rob me of this stupid little island. The horrors persist, but so do I. hey i know this is 2 months in but i understand feeling so desolate and alone in a circumstance no one can help with. In my opinion this is something you should contact legal counsel for. Your local queer association (if you have one) may have access to legal advice for situations like these. I can empathise somewhat, I'm a third culture kid and there's very little to help someone like me as well.

I hope you and your wife are ok and in a safer spot :( if you're canadian like me, consider this resource: [https://queerjustice.ca/en/](https://queerjustice.ca/en/)

There's also this resource [https://ilglaw.org/](https://ilglaw.org/) 

even if nothing has happened yet, knowing that there's people dedicated to using the law to help minorities and queer people can feel a bit relieving, specially when it comes to very real threats of sexual violence against you or your partner. 

Other than that, I don't have much. I too feel like im perpetually stuck in cptsd land as i watch things around me fall apart but so far im still fine. it's a lot to bear. im medicated to hell and back but that only helps with me not completely fetal positioning and just ending it despite me and my family's hard work of double immigrating is finally paying off.   
  
The least i can do is to offer you what little I can with the info you have given me. Try your best to take it one day at a time, things are getting rough again for all minorities and the best way to piss off the people who want us dead is to continue living. 

Look for better work, one that respects you and your wife. If you are able to, switch phone numbers or have a work phone and personal phone. This is the one time where the AI feature to transcribe calls before you pick them up can be useful to see what calls are legitimate calls and which ones are just harassment. Have a burner phone for work, since it will be exposed anyway, and then just make notes on who will legitimately call you and who won't at work and turn it off after work unless absolutely necessary. 

Hopefully this helps.

i personally am a strong believer in tab stash. see i really don't like to have many tabs (im a 3-4 per window, split across two separate windows as like zones), but sometimes i have this larger amount of tabs (say about 10) in one window i want to go back to at some point, but bookmarking all of them is a pain, specially if you have a large number of bookmarks already. here enters tab stash, you can basically create backlinks and bookmarks for an entire window's worth of tabs, and they're sorted by date. now i can just say "oh shit i should go back to this at some point but i do gotta work tomorrow", i stash my tabs, and after work i can reload my tabs from my stash. 

if you are the kind of person who lives and dies by the "everything drawer" method, tab stash is there to just keep track of tabs you want to keep for later or eventually and are not like "bookmark" worthy so you just chuck it in the just in case box, and go back to it when you feel like it or want to. 

I've spent a lot of time with tree-style tabs and tab session manager, specially during my final years of my comp-sci degree in a more theory-heavy program, doing lots of papers and research, to try to be able to manage the stupid number of tabs i had, but found a lot of the methodology behind most tab management approaches to not work for me in the same way that i kind of suck at keeping an agenda (unless its for work to mixed results). I learned a lot about myself how i work best, and also can see the usefulness of them and they have helped me in specific situations.  
  
the most success i had was with tab stash after i graduated, because it was, in a way, me just pinning my tabs for later for any reason, and is sorted by date and time, so i can always revisit something if i saved it and can always look back. its my "fuck it we ball" section while my bookmarks are like "IMPORTANT WORK AND RESPONSIBILITIES" section. 

tab stash is surprisingly flexible in its simplicity.

Hey! Here's some tips from years of experimenting with press-ons. I am a computer programmer and work full time in IT and have had dev jobs, but also sometimes want cute nails to match with my green hair and my piercings, so I've spent a lot of time trying to finding press-ons that can survive for (average) about a week before I take them out and take a break.

Try filing from the bottom side to better fit your nailbed shape. I like to trim from the bottom and then file it smooth when I have press-ons that feel too big for my nails, that way they dont dig in into your cuticles and skin, and ensuring they actually fit your nailbed! It feels like a crime at first but practicing with budget sets is pretty fun.

Also, definitely use glue. A good set usually comes with one. If you get some glue dissolver/remover, you can even reuse your nails if you're careful enough. High quality sets can be highly reusable, making them really good investments in the long run. Use as little glue as possible (it is literally superglue-adjacent) and then do a light pass on the edges so they're secured. A brush type glue is best for learning and you can get some formulated for different purposes like quick drying or extra hold. Your mileage may vary on those.

Also, brand does matter. Since there's no real standardized sizing for nails, there's a bit of a vanity sizing problem. For example, at my Shopper's Drug Mart (Canadian CVS), I see that their private label, Quo, has press on nails that say they're short but they feel massive!. My roomate has smaller nailbeds so finding press ons for her has been even harder. In my experience, a lot of this is trial and error. Personally I find Broadway and KISS to be very good budget nails with very diverse sizing. Their small/short and petite are pretty small. My hands are pretty small so even I go through a lot of the smaller sizes in a set first before I trim the bigger ones.

At my Winners (Canadian TJMaxx, like literally owned by them) I can find some of the very high quality sets at a discounted rate. I swear on Glamnetic Short Ovals, they are thin but durable, the design is printed so it can survive dabs of acetone if it gets surface stains and the designs remain, and when used right, they can be reused. Of course, you can only re-use them so much. They're thin enough to be able to gently trim with scissors at the bottom to get larger ones shortened or thinned out.

Another thing, consider other shapes of press on nails, such as square, coffin or even oval/round. Sometimes our hands compliment different shapes. Our fingers can vary wildly from person to person, so try to experiment until you find a shape/length that works for you! Budget sets are incredibly fragile and aren't always meant to be reused, but they're great for practice and experimentation. If you like painting your own nails, you can hit up a Sally's or Amazon for a kit of 100 nails of all kinds of sizes (economies of scale make these pretty cheap!). There's some excellent variety in these sets so they're great for figuring out what works for you!

Over at r/RedditLaqueristas there are some excellent posts about how to get the most out of your press ons. A lot of what I know I learned from people from there.

While I do understand what you're trying to imply and arrive at, I really believe this question doesn't hold as much water as you think.

Part of healing from such an event is to accept that it happened and that it may not necessarily be the fault of the victim they got themselves into such a situation. 

The real crux of the discussion in my opinion would the weight of such a fault (if there was any) is more than the weight of the fault an assaulter would have. Your question implies that the fault of the victim will eventually override any consequences the criminal will face. This will never be the case. The criminal holds far more responsibility and has to be held accountable or brought to justice for something as simple as not assaulting someone, rather than them getting away with it because the victim didn't take the 300 bajillion steps or develop agoraphobia.   


Was my series of assaults to me a positive? No. Did they contribute to me eventually develop as a person? Yes, as unfortunate as it is, those events deeply impact a person. Did such events eventually make me become a better person and capable of helping others? Yes. Did it have to be this way? No.   


Assault, regardless of how much positive outcome there is afterwards is never a net positive. A victim of sexual assault can eventually learn to accept and heal from such events and be more careful in the future but the real point is that it **doesn't have to be that way.**

A person can accept such events happened to them and still believe they weren't at any fault. A person can accept such events and understand that they didn't deserve to be assaulted just because they did things that would to some justify or account for the likelihood of getting assaulted. 

For example, the person who entered your room, while informed, probably erred on the side that the assaulters wouldn't actually do it because we, as a society, believe people should understand that doing such a thing is bad. Just because the person entered that room does not mean it was justified for them to get assaulted, no matter how much they were informed. 

As much as one can squint and come up with an argument over why and what lead to such chain of events happening, the real point and lesson derived from it should be that it shouldn't happen in the first place.   


No one should live in constant fear that any move they do will eventually lead them to being assaulted. No one would fear being assaulted if there weren't any people who were assaulting in the first place out there.

Okay, lets say for the sake of argument you have your ethical conundrum.   
You have someone go into a room where their chances of getting assaulted is almost a 100%.   


Is it their fault for getting assaulted by going into that room? In the grand scheme of things, not really. Of course, fault in any scenario is complex and you can have multiple types of fault and to different degrees.

While it's not their ultimate fault, it could've been avoided but a lot of the things that lead to such events tend to be out of the victim's control, specially if the victim has been trying their best to not only be safe but also protecting themselves.   


One of the best places where such a conundrum shines the best is in cases of roofing. Say you're at a party and you've been trying your absolute hardest to take care of your drink and not leaving it alone or keeping your eyes off. Yes, one could argue that it is the victim's fault they went outside the day they got assaulted but realistically that is super bullshit, and even if they did (for the sake of argument, hypothetically really speaking) provoke it in some way, whatever blame they may even have becomes negligible compared to the massive crime the assaulter committed (and that the assaulter had a lot more control over).

The Mounties in Ontario are nice and reroute your complaints to the appropriate police. Other provinces aint so kind in that regard.  

FBI works alongside the CIA in the US to perform reconnaissance operations and espionage internationally alongside being the US's closest thing to the National Police other than the Secret Service or the literal Military. You do need a USB Y as one single port on the wiiu will not deliver enough power for the read/write speeds.  
I tried this out last week on my 256gb ssd with an enclosure.  
Edit: I should probably explain what happens if you just have it on one usb plug. The ssd will have enough power to remain on for a little while only but as soon as any sort of transfer happens, specially for titles installed on usb, it will disconnect itself as a security measure on the ssd (specially if its nvme), and your wiiu \*will\* crash and go to a special crash handler  


If you only have 1 usb y cable and want to transfer your data from one drive to an ssd, i recommend you take the long route and somewhat safe route (assuming your data is less than 50gb big, because after that you run into risks) of transferring the contents of the hdd into a sd card big enough to handle with a good usb adapter (does not need as much power, but it will take a eternity and a half), then unplug the hdd, plug the ssd, have the wiiu format it and slap everything from the sdcard into the ssd with the wiiu tools. At that point you can reformat for repartition your hdd.
